reader.requirement: At --std 85, after a DELETE, READ, REWRITE, START or WRITE on an indexed file that ends without an invalid key condition but with another exception condition (3x, 4x, 9x), the INVALID KEY phrase must not run, the NOT INVALID KEY phrase must not run, the I-O status (and FILE STATUS item) is updated, any applicable USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure (file-name or open-mode) runs, and control then goes on as the USE statement's rules say (to the end of the statement).

edition-consulted.switches: >>TURN is refused before 2002, so ec.IoMaskFor(file) is 0 at 85 and EmitUseHook always takes the plain __IoCheck arm with NotPhraseGate null
DialectLevel >= 2002 adds the SORT GR17 exit filter around an EC-free USE procedure; 85 takes the plain try/finally (irrelevant to an explicit I-O statement)

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|CobolVersion|Edition.|DialectBehavior over UseTierEmitter, DispatchEmitter, EcEmitter, SequentialIoEmitter, KeyedIoEmitter, IoStatusClass; UseTierEmitter documents the tiers as edition-invariant (kb/Work PB344).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f16_03 covers 47/48/49 on a dynamic file with a file-name USE; not covered: 44 (RECORD VARYING), 43 on REWRITE in sequential access, an open-mode (ON INPUT) USE, and a file with no applicable USE but a FILE STATUS item

probes.printed: USE-A 44 / A44 44 (WRITE of 3 chars under VARYING 4 TO 10 with INVALID KEY + NOT INVALID KEY: neither phrase ran)
probes.expected: 44 is a logic error (§1985:IX.1.3.4 GRL2.5 d), not an invalid key: the USE procedure runs, no phrase runs

probes.printed: USE-A 43 / A43 43; contrast REWRITE with changed key: IK-21 21 / A21 21 (no USE); C47 47 on a closed file with no applicable USE (neither phrase)
probes.expected: 43: USE runs, IK not run; 21 is an invalid key so IK runs and USE does not; 47 with nothing applicable: status updated, control to the next statement

probes.printed: USE-INPUT 48 / B48 48; USE-INPUT 49 / B49 49 (random-access indexed file open INPUT, open-mode USE ON INPUT)
probes.expected: the open-mode USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure runs for WRITE (48) and DELETE (49); no INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: >>TURN directive requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: no compiler-directive facility in 1985; the EC-I-O checking arm of the hook is unreachable at 85

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.1.3.5 GRL2.1  (1.3.5 The Invalid Key Condition)  the text is in GRL2.1

reader.notes: The INVALID KEY arm is gated on status '2x' only (IoStatusClass.InvalidKey) and the plain __IoCheck suppresses the USE selection only for a 2x when the phrase is written, so every other unsuccessful family reaches the file-name or open-mode tier. All six witnesses and four probes match the 1985 text.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-090: r1_global.cob (nested program R1INNER, the only USE is USE GLOBAL ... ON I-O / ON OUTPUT in the containing program): DELETE with no prior READ (43) -> USE-GLOBAL-IO, A-DEL 43; WRITE to a sequential-access file open I-O (48) with INVALID KEY + NOT INVALID KEY -> USE-GLOBAL-IO, A-WR 48, neither phrase; START and READ on a dynamic file open OUTPUT (47) with both phrases -> USE-GLOBAL-OUTPUT, 47, neither phrase; control returns to the statement after the I-O statement. r1b_91.cob: WRITE of a native character of ordinal 1001 (implementor 9x, status 91) with both phrases -> USE-FX 91 / AFTER-X 91 (neither phrase); same on a file with no USE -> AFTER-Y 91. The first r1 run also showed DELETE ... INVALID KEY on a sequential-access file refused (COBOL1720), as §1985:IX.4.3.3 SR1 requires. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.1.3.5 GRL2.1 the text is in GRL2.1; OK §1985:IX.4.3.3 SR1 the text is in SR1. Grep of SequentialIoEmitter/KeyedIoEmitter/IoStatusClass for DialectLevel|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior: only the file registrations and SelectWhenOnlyForFilePhraseStatements (not on this path).
